author: Doezer
tooling: manual assessment, cross-referenced with npm audit and Anchore Grype/Trivy scans of the published container image

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable function is RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature VERIFICATION in node-forge (forge.pki.verify / certificate.verify): a malformed nested DigestAlgorithm lets a forged signature pass verification against a low-exponent RSA public key (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33894). Questarr uses node-forge only in server/ssl.ts, for (1) generating an RSA key pair (pki.rsa.generateKeyPair), (2) creating and signing the self-signed TLS certificate the setup wizard can generate (pki.createCertificate + certificate.sign — signature creation, not verification), and (3) parsing PEM certificates to display expiry/subject in the UI (pki.certificateFromPem). It never calls the verification API — the certificate/key match check in validateCertFiles() uses Node's own tls.createSecureContext — so the vulnerable code path is unreachable from Questarr, and no Questarr input can be routed through it.
statements.action_statement: No patched release exists as of 2026-10-03 (node-forge 1.4.0 is the latest published version, and the advisory's affected range is <=1.4.0). Re-assess whenever a new node-forge release ships (Dependabot proposes upgrades); when a fixed version is available, upgrade and replace this statement with a `fixed` statement. This statement is invalid if Questarr ever starts verifying signatures with node-forge — that change must be paired with a patched or replacement dependency before it ships.
